title: Vilasa 18. Gopala Bhatta; the Deliverance of Chand Raya
html:
On the followers of the Gosvamis of Vrindavana — Kashishvara, Lokanatha, Raghunatha Dasa and Krishnadasa Kaviraja; Mahaprabhu's meeting with Gopala Bhatta at Srirangam, his journey to Vrindavana and the Hari-bhakti-vilasa; the disciples of Gopala Bhatta and the fall of Harivamsha; Narottama drives a brahma-daitya out of the sinner Chand Raya and initiates him, his brother Santosha and his father Raghavendra; Chand Raya at Kheturi; captivity under the Nawab, the subduing of the elephant and release; the author's closing words

1Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu Sri Krishna Chaitanya!
Glory, glory to Nityananda, whose heart is compassion!

2Glory, glory to Advaitachandra, the utmost of mercy,
who, bringing down Gaurachandra, fulfilled his desire!

3Glory, glory to Gadadhara, the ocean of rasa!
Glory, glory to the devotees of Gaura, possessed of every virtue!

4Of all the Gosanis who live in Vrindavana,
whose branches and sub-branches they are, I have not written.

5Whoever has written of it wrote by consulting the shastras;
but I write following the command of Prabhu1.

6My Thakurani holds within her the shakti of Sri Gauranga;
all that I have written I wrote on hearing the command from her blessed lips.

7As Gauranga spoke, so [speaks] the Thakurani;
I know no other view — that alone I expound.

8My Thakurani is she who sports in Vrindavana;
of that I have not written, knowing her heart2.

9To write disputes on siddhanta is an offence;
[but here are] words from Prabhu's blessed lips — in this there is no fear.

10Two brothers born of one mother — Rupa and Sanatana;
Prabhu placed his own shakti in them.

11Rupa and Sanatana are devoted to Prabhu's feet;
Sanatana and Rupa are shown the highest honour and esteem.

12In the land of Mathura, Kashishvara Pandita is renowned;
his devotion to Rupa and Sanatana is very deep.

13I write the reason for it, I write it once more:
he is a disciple of Ishvara Puri — such is [his standing]3.

14[Ishvara Puri] entrusted him to Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
[and Prabhu] wove him [into his tree] as one of his chief branches.

15Gadadhara Pandita is Prabhu's own shakti;
not seeing Vidyanidhi, Prabhu wept bitterly4.

16Gadadhara Pandita is the disciple of that same Pundarika,
and Bhugarbha is his disciple, especially dear to Prabhu.

17Rupa and Sanatana honour him and show him kindness;
to some he shows love and devotion, to others compassion.

18Lokanatha Gosani is the vessel of Prabhu's mercy;
he delivers souls — compassion incarnate.

19Rupa and Sanatana revere him as the foremost [of devotees];
there is no other so renounced in the three worlds.

20He takes no thought for food and lives in a secluded place;
no one knows in what sadhana his time passes.

21Rupa and Sanatana hold him a worthy perfected soul;
when they ask him, he answers, and they accept [his word]5.

22His servant [and disciple] is Thakura Mahashaya;
how many are his virtues — how could I write them?

23Kashishvara has a disciple, a resident of Vraja,
born in a brahmana family, named Bhaktakashi.

24Govinda Gosani and Yadava Acharya,
leaving their household affairs, took shelter at his feet.

25These two brahmana youths, natives of Gauda,
live with their master and serve him.

26Krishna Pandita Thakura is a pure Vrajavasi;
Rupa and Sanatana show him great honour.

27The glory of Kashishvara and Krishnadasa is boundless;
Sri Rupa Gosani knows their glory6.

28Keli-kala and Kunkuma — such are the svarupas of these two7;
the two, the life of all, came together.

29Raghunatha Bhatta, dear [to Prabhu], whose life is Gauranga,
stays constantly with Rupa and Sanatana.

30Sri Yadunandana is a disciple of Acharya Gosani;
Raghunatha Dasa is [his] disciple, wholly surrendered8.

31By the strength of Nityananda's mercy he gave up worldly wealth,
went to Nilachala and saw Prabhu.

32With utmost renunciation he lived with [Prabhu] in the Kshetra;
seeing him, Prabhu was filled with joy and delight.

33After some days [Prabhu] entrusted him to Svarupa,
who trained him in body, speech and mind.

34Only Gauranga himself understood the reason:
why he did so — who can understand?

35[Svarupa] is most skilled in the charming rasa of shringara;
night and day he assists [Prabhu], [endowed with] the qualities of Lalita9.

36The former word is fulfilled — who can understand it?
As one dear to Svarupa, [Prabhu] shows [Raghunatha] mercy10.

37After some more days, that Raghunatha Dasa
[Prabhu], giving him a garland of gunja, placed in Radha's hands.

38He gave him the stone of Govardhana to serve
and ordered him to go to Vrindavana.

39[There] he surrendered himself to Rupa and Sanatana
and so was united with his own perfected yutha11.

40They became very kind to him, [holding him] dear as life:
this one shows devotion, those embrace him.

41He chose to dwell by the kunda of Radhika;
fifty-six dandas of the day and night are his bhajana12.

42Who else is so renounced and so dear to Radhika?
The Kaviraja, his disciple, lived beside him13.

43For the fulfilment of his own cherished goal [he chose] such a mahashaya —
[so] writes Yadunandana himself, my guru14.

44When Krishnadasa Kaviraja [lived] in the land of Gauda,
he performed bhajana to Krishna, absorbed in bliss.

45One day, in a village called Jhamatpur,
Nityananda, the abode of virtues, appeared to him,

46with his companions, in a captivating dress.
Seeing his form, Krishnadasa rejoiced at heart.

47Bowing down, he offered him much praise.
The command came: "All perfection [is yours] — go to Vrindavana!"

48In his own book he writes of himself as Prabhu's disciple:
"Not regarding that I am lowly and wretched, he showed me mercy"15.

49Then he went again to Vrindavana
and took shelter at the feet of Raghunatha.

50Why he writes so, why he takes [another] shelter —
only one of great realization understands.

51Such is the conduct of the perfected, utterly pure:
when one takes shelter in bhava, all things are revealed.

52For that virtue Rupa and Sanatana showed him mercy.
Thus I have described [their] views.

53Hear now about Gopala Bhatta:
how he went to Vrindavana and how he found shelter.

54When Mahaprabhu travelled to the south,
wandering, he came to Ranga-kshetra16.

55Bathing in the Kaveri and seeing Ranganatha,
he took his alms in the house of Trimalla Bhatta17.

56Out of love for the Bhatta, Prabhu spent the chaturmasya there18;
day and night he spoke of Krishna with the Bhatta.

57Formerly [the family] worshipped Lakshmi-Narayana;
in jest Prabhu raised [this] question with him:

58"Lakshmi, who dwells on her Lord's chest, though a faithful wife,
desires the company of Krishna — so the shastras say.

59Why, being a faithful wife, does she long for Krishna's company?"
Having said this, Mahaprabhu smiled softly.

60Hearing this, the Bhatta was bewildered:
he could not grasp the inner meaning.

61Afraid at heart, he said to Prabhu:
"Whatever you say, my mind cannot enter into it.

62I know nothing of the goal and the means;
I know that you are that very Lakshmi-Narayana.

63Showing me mercy, you have come here
and appeared to me in the dress of a sannyasi.

64What praise can I offer? Nothing comes to mind.
Knowing me ignorant, show me mercy, O Merciful One!"

65Hearing this, Mahaprabhu was moved to mercy;
embracing him, he imparted shakti to him.

66At that moment the Vraja-lila was revealed in his mind;
his body swelled with prema and he began to dance.

67Prabhu showed him his own form
and commanded: "All the people in your house —

68bring them all, let them see me now."
Hearing Prabhu's command, the Bhatta went

69and brought before Prabhu the whole household —
two brothers, his son and all who lived in the house.

70Prabhu in his mercy purified their minds;
seeing Prabhu's form, all shed tears.

71All fell to the ground, prostrating themselves;
in his mercy he placed his feet on everyone's head.

72All went home; three remained.
Mercifully Prabhu spoke sweet words:

73"This son of yours, named Gopala Bhatta —
my great mercy rests upon him.

74Have him taught and make him a fine pandita;
do not have him married — this I tell you."

75Smiling, Prabhu looked at Prabodhananda:
"Your disciple will be a treasury of virtues in all the shastras"19.

76Gopala Bhatta was then studying the Sri Bhagavata;
Prabhu told him his own inner view.

77He said to him: "You will remain at home for some time;
when you are parted from your mother and father, you will go to Vrindavana.

78There you will find great happiness — this I tell you."
Having said this to him, he said to Prabodhananda:

79"Be sure to send him to Vrindavana:
I have need of him — this I tell you."

80Saying this, Prabhu took his leave;
in separation from Prabhu, weeping arose in the Bhatta's house.

81That Prabodhananda was dear to Prabhu as life;
in his mercy Prabhu made him the best of bhagavatas.

82Thus I have described such mercy of Prabhu;
in passing I have written all this account.

83Here is the account of what I have written;
now I write of Gopala Bhatta's going to Vrindavana.

84At the end of his days Prabodhananda remembered [this]
and, calling the Bhatta, told him Prabhu's words.

85[Gopala] remembered the command [Prabhu] had spoken
and resolved in his mind: "I will go to Vrindavana."

86Prabodhananda Sarasvati showed him mercy;
[Gopala] himself wrote [of this] in the book Hari-bhakti-vilasa20.

87At the end of his days Sarasvati said:
"Go and take shelter of Rupa and Sanatana."

88When his mind had turned away from samsara,
[Prabodhananda] wrote a letter with his own hand.

89He wrote a fitting letter to the two Gosanis:
"I have sent Gopala Bhatta to you."

90With that letter [Gopala] set out by the road through Jharikhanda
and after some days arrived at Mathura.

91The next day in Vrindavana he saw Rupa,
bowed down and offered him much praise.

92He gave the letter; the two brothers read it and understood all,
kept him near them and showed him great mercy.

93The two brothers loved the Bhatta as their life;
after some days the two brothers gave him a command —

94[to compose] the book Hari-bhakti-vilasa on Vaishnava conduct,
on the rites of Vaishnavas, mudras, rules and the rest.

95The book was completed and he offered it to Sanatana;
he accepted it, making it his own book.

96In it he wrote a praise of his own guru —
the first shloka of the book, the auspicious invocation21.

97He is perfected, his deeds cannot be understood;
whoever thinks of them otherwise brings harm on himself22.

98Taking into account each one's virtues and nature,
he shows mercy accordingly, knowing his mind.

99What were the names of Gopala Bhatta's disciples,
and in what land each lived — hear the account.

100Srinivasa Acharya, Harivamsha the Vrajavasi,
Gopinatha Pujari — a great treasury of virtues23.

101And two more disciples of the Bhatta, a great treasury of prema —
Shambhurama and Makaranda, natives of Gujarat.

102The service of Sri Radha-ramana he entrusted to Gopinatha24.
These are the disciples of the Bhatta told of in the account.

103Not heeding his guru's command, Harivamsha fell:
all the virtues he had came to ruin.

104For what reason Harivamsha fell
I shall describe, expanding on it a little.

105Harivamsha the Vrajavasi was very learned;
he constantly served the Bhatta Gosvami.

106The Bhatta Gosvami had great love for him:
[he was] a supreme devotee, the abode of all virtues.

107[But] by fate he transgressed his guru's command.
Listen, listen, O hearers, with minds attentive!

108One day, on the day of Sri Ekadashi, Harivamsha
came to Prabhu chewing betel.

109Seeing betel in his mouth, the Gosani asked him [about it];
he answered: "It is Sri Radha's prasada betel."

110The Gosani said: "On the day of Sri Ekadashi
one must abstain even from Hari's prasada.

111As it is said:
'Hari's prasada is always to be accepted, except on Ekadashi.'"25

112The Gosani said: "Do not do such a thing again:
by transgressing the shastras you will commit an offence."

113Bowing to the Gosani, Harivamsha went away from there,
but, fond of betel, he could not give it up.

114Again on Ekadashi, having chewed Sri Radha's prasada betel,
he went to the Gosvami.

115Harivamsha bowed to the Gosani,
and he saw his lips reddened with betel.

116The Gosani said: "Harivamsha, you are a pandita —
why do you act contrary [to the rules]?

117Chewing betel on the day of Sri Ekadashi —
[by this] you have taken all sins upon yourself.

118Being a pandita, you have broken the command;
for this offence I reject you."

119Harivamsha said: "Taking betel is my service;
I cannot refuse this prasada.

120I have committed an offence at your lotus feet,
[but] I could not disregard Sri Radha's prasada."

121Hearing these words, the Gosani became angry,
and Harivamsha quickly went away from there.

122Harivamsha lost the service of Radha-ramana
and manifested the image of Sri Radha-vallabha26.

123In that offending body two sons were born to him,
named Vanachandra and Vrindavanachandra.

124Earlier Harivamsha had had two other sons,
who were given the names Krishnadasa and Suryadasa.

125Entrusting the service to his sons, he went to the forest,
immersing his mind in the feet of Sri Radha-vallabha.

126Strange are the ways of fate — they cannot be understood:
robbers cut off Harivamsha's head and threw it into the Yamuna.

127Crying "Radha, Radha!", the head floated upstream
to where Gopala Bhatta Gosani was bathing.

128At that ghat the head came to rest
and, crying "Radha", began to shed tears.

129At that time the Bhatta Gosani was at that ghat
and was amazed that a severed head was saying "Radha".

130Looking closely, the Gosani saw Harivamsha's head;
he said, "Come, come!" and felt great pain at heart.

131The severed head came and touched Prabhu's feet:
"Tell me, will you forgive the offence of an offender?"

132The Gosani said: "I have forgiven your offence" —
and with these words he placed his foot on its head.

133Receiving [the touch of] his foot, Harivamsha was liberated.
Gopala Bhatta told everyone all that had happened.

134When the one against whom the offence was committed forgives,
then Sri Krishna's mercy comes — let all know this.

135One whose offence is not removed,
even if a great devotee, will not obtain Krishna's mercy.

136The offence of an offender does not leave even his descendants;
for this reason Vaishnavas should shun them.

137Sri Jiva Gosani is the disciple of Sri Rupa;
know this in due order — there is no other27.

138Their comings and goings are for Gauranga's happiness;
their bhajana and remembrance are for Prabhu's own happiness.

139Whatever bhajana and shelter each has had from the first —
as the devotee is in each place, so is the way.

140The wish-fulfilling tree named Chaitanya bears five fruits28;
know, all of you — [they are tasted] in the company of those devotees.

141Everyone's inclination of mind and dharma are preserved;
and the accompanying disciples, too, they blessed with mercy.

142Srinivasa and Narottama are the two empowered ones;
both have countless branches — I cannot tell them all.

143The number of branches and virtues of these two I cannot write;
through that door all the lowly and wretched are delivered.

144[This is] the description of this virtue of Thakura Mahashaya;
hear also another wondrous word.

145He in whose heart Gauranga himself dwells
serves outwardly there too that image of prema.

146Yatras, great festivals, service [of the deity], service of Vaishnavas,
bhajana and remembrance — so he spends his time.

147Those who became his disciples he instructs:
"Serve Krishna and perform bhajana to Krishna"29.

148"The word of my Prabhu is within me and without;
[all is] that Prabhu, that command — if he shows mercy."

149Narottama considers himself unworthy:
"Listen, disciples and friends, I tell you:

150one whose aim from the very first is to attain Krishna's feet
should take for himself a count of a lakh of names"30.

151His branches multiplied in his own land and in other lands.
I shall write one more account, full of bliss.

152Raghavendra Raya, a brahmana, a resident of a certain land —
I shall tell of him, [beginning] from Garerhat31.

153He had two sons, Santosha and Chand Raya;
all people spoke of Chand Raya as mighty.

154A great warrior, strong, valiant in battle —
hearing his name, [people] trembled for their lives.

155He was the zamindar [of an estate] of eighty-four thousand [rupees]32.
After some time it came about thus:

156[The land] passed to Garhi-dvara: there [sat] a faujdar;
setting up a thana at Rajmahal, he governed [the land]33.

157[Chand Raya], seeing himself strong, reasoned in his mind:
he pays no tax to the Padshah and sets up his own posts in the villages.

158He keeps five thousand horse and some foot;
by force of arms he seized many lands.

159He gave battle — the people in fear abandoned the thana;
he plundered and carried off all the money and wealth.

160The land became the domain of his fort — so he lives34:
robbing, stealing, killing people, heeding no one.

161His sins cannot be written;
people stop their ears and run away.

162Worshipping Shakti, he constantly drinks wine and eats meat;
he plunders others' wives, homes and goods and carries them off.

163At the festival of Durga he worships the image,
and there is no end to the animals he slaughters.

164In the abode of Yama, Chitragupta cannot write down
all his sins — hundreds of bundles have piled up35.

165One day Chitragupta says to the king [Yama]:
"What do these two brahmana sons not do!

166Having committed so many sins, where will they stay?
How long will the two of them suffer hell?

167I remember the two of old, Jagai and Madhai;
these two brothers are greater sinners still.

168Those were great sinners, but did not commit so many sins."
King Yama said: "Shame on them!"

169Thus Chand Raya lived for some time.
[Then] a brahma-daitya came and seized him36.

170That brahmana son was exceedingly wicked;
[the spirit], entering his body, beats him.

171It binds his body; [Chand Raya] raves incessantly;
his body has withered — he is about to give up his life.

172His father brings many physicians from land after land;
many remedies were tried — the spirit leaves for none of them.

173He summoned an astrologer37, who made his reckoning:
"The brahma-daitya will not leave — hear, this is certain."

174Reckoning again, he said: "Listen, sir:
there is no remedy — [there is] one, but it is impossible.

175The zamindar of the land of Kheturi
has a son — Narottama, Thakura Mahashaya.

176If he in his mercy comes [here],
then the spirit will leave" — so he declared.

177Hearing this, his father summoned a pandita
and had a fitting letter written by his hand.

178Separately the Raya wrote [to Krishnananda] with a request:
"By my good fortune may your son come [to us]."

179[Setting out] the reason he wrote, having considered everything,
he sent [for him] a sukhpal and bearers38.

180All those men went to Kheturi,
gave the letter to the Majumdar and made their request.

181Having read it, he pondered the matter;
with the letter he went to where Thakura Mahashaya was.

182Holding the letter he had read in his hand, he said [to himself]:
"Why did they send the letter? They have troubled themselves in vain.

183Who has the courage to tell him and send him there?"
To Narottama he said nothing of this matter39.

184Out of fear the Raya told [him] nothing; going outside,
he wrote a reply and sent it off.

185The men came and reported everything to him;
hearing it, [Chand Raya's] father began to weep:

186"Mother Durga, save my son this time!
Besides you, who has the power to protect?"

187At night the Thakurani, in the guise of a brahmana woman40,
spoke to Chand Raya, smiling softly:

188"What good can there be, son? Your body is full of sin;
I have no power to do this.

189Of all the sinful deeds and sinful ways in the world —
who but you does such things?

190You did not worship Krishna's feet; you did such things;
you worshipped me — my heart breaks with grief.

191Whoever leaves Krishna and worships me, the world becomes his enemy;
I destroy him — I cannot bear it.

192Whoever worships me out of greed, his next life is ruined:
[I] take away his wealth and livelihood, and then comes utter ruin.

193My lord (Shiva) is intoxicated with Krishna's qualities;
offering everything to Him, he remains in meditation41.

194The Three-eyed, Five-faced one [lives] for His sake,
and I am his maidservant, I tell you42.

195You two brothers took shelter of me,
[but] on what you have done there is no mercy of mine.

196When I am worshipped in sattva-guna, I am glad;
at rajo-guna and tamo-guna my breast is torn.

197Krishna is the maker of the world, the shastras say;
who else on earth grants liberation and bhakti?

198You have reached the limit of sin — there is no talking of it;
King Yama and Chitragupta are in great distress.

199Having sinned, how will you two endure the reckoning?
In the records there are bundles as high as a mountain.

200My lord will be pleased [only] then:
without delay, son, worship the feet of Govinda.

201Thakura Mahashaya, of whom the astrologer spoke —
bring him and take shelter at his feet.

202Srinivasa's disciple Sri Govinda Kaviraja
worshipped me, leaving all else aside43;

203he begged me much for liberation,
but to give it was not in my power.

204Taking shelter at the Acharya's feet,
he gained bhakti to Krishna and dispelled the fear of samsara.

205That Srinivasa and Narottama are one life;
for the sake of the lila two bodies exist.

206To deliver the souls of the Kali age, Chaitanya and Nitai
came to earth together with their associates and attendants.

207They delivered all souls by giving them Krishna's name;
from the prema of those two are Srinivasa and Narottama.

208Whoever worships these two knowing them to be one
will surely attain the feet of Govinda.

209Whoever, seeing them as different, reviles or honours them [apart]44,
know for certain, sinks into Yama's noose and perishes."

210Having said this, the Thakurani vanished;
in [Chand Raya's] heart an astonished understanding arose.

211In the morning he told everything to his father and brother:
"Bring the Thakura — then my life will be spared."

212In the morning [they sent] two brahmanas with a letter:
"You are merciful — show mercy to me, your servant.

213When I see those two feet with my own eyes,
then this wicked brahmana will tell you everything."

214With the letter the two brahmanas go to the village of Kheturi;
setting down the letter, the two brahmanas bowed.

215[Narottama] honoured them and [asked] whence they had come.
"Here is the letter — what more need we say?"

216He gave the brahmanas food and gave them lodging;
reading the letter, he considered its words.

217He told the Kaviraja all the news:
"Consider this and tell me your opinion."

218[He replied:] "This is a very hard matter, beyond people's understanding;
what can I say? You possess all virtues,

219you hold every power, the manifest image of prema:
to see you with one's eyes is joy and delight."

220Thus, deliberating, part of the night passed.
Gaura-raya himself, sitting on his seat, speaks45:

221"Listen, Narottama, I tell you what to do:
this is no great wonder — go to him.

222Those two brahmanas are the greatest of sinners;
for the sake of seeing you [Chand Raya] keeps hold of life.

223Show him mercy, let him be delivered;
the brahma-daitya will leave him — this is my command.

224You have appeared for the deliverance of sinners:
many, receiving salvation, will become servants of Krishna.

225Take the Kaviraja with you and go to his house:
how many hearts will be filled with joy!"

226Morning came; Prabhu's command became [his] strength;
he told the Kaviraja everything that had happened.

227Having taken their morning bath, the two are setting out;
at that moment the Majumdar arrives.

228[Narottama] told him all about the letter:
"I think I shall go to his house."

229The Raya said: "It is his fortune [earned] over many births
that he will see those feet of yours with his own eyes.

230I, luckless one, shall not see it;
how the mercy is given I shall hear afterwards."

231He arranged [a party], giving many men as escort;
[Narottama] sets out with the Kaviraja, taking Vaishnavas with him.

232Bowing to Gauranga, he went out;
all the people weep, unable to restrain themselves.

233Honouring everyone, he set off;
behind him walk those two brahmanas.

234That day, seeing a village [on the way], they halted on the road;
one brahmana went [ahead] with the news.

235He told the Raya everything, the reason for the journey;
he rejoiced at heart, and his eyes overflowed.

236With brahmanas, worthy men and a great crowd,
joyful at heart, he went out on the road to meet him.

237How many instruments sound — who can count?
Going a little way, all of them saw [the Thakura].

238Seeing his form, with tears they fell at his feet;
smiling, he greeted them all.

239When he arrived and entered the village,
the people gaze at him, absorbed in bliss.

240Full pitchers have been set here and there along the road,
hundreds of banana trees have been planted.

241Flower garlands at every house, along every street;
thousands of people are following him.

242All the women raise the auspicious ululation46;
people count themselves blessed and their lives fulfilled.

243They gaze at his form — streams of tears flow;
hearing [of him], people from other villages run with loud cries.

244Then he went to the Raya's house;
[the Raya], joyful at heart, washed his feet.

245Gazing at his form, [the Raya] shed streams of tears;
he washed the Thakura's feet with water.

246[The Thakura] sat on the seat; the Raya says to the Thakura:
"There are no words for the limit of my fortune"47.

247"Good, good," the Thakura said to him,
"I shall see your son. Come, in which room is he?"

248To where Chand Raya lies on his bed
the Thakura goes with all the people.

249The Raya went and raised him, taking him in his arms.
The Thakura entered that room.

250The Thakura's companions stood in front;
Chand Raya sees [the Thakura] with his own eyes.

251The brahma-daitya that was in his heart
began to speak, shouting aloud:

252"Having committed many sins, I became a brahma-daitya;
such a sinner as I am, such a sinner I found.

253For so many days I have enjoyed myself in his body;
now I am commanded — where am I to go?"

254In the midst of all the people he spoke again:
"I have been granted the sight of you — may I be delivered!

255You are the purifier of the fallen: by the mere sight of you
even a brahma-daitya is delivered — I have understood the reason.

256Kheturi is not a village, it is Gupta Vrindavana;
when [my] reckoning is spent, [may I] be born in that land,

257and, being born, take shelter at your feet —
then mercy will surely come to this lowly one."

258Thakura Mahashaya said: "Listen, king of spirits:
leave his heart at once and go."

259The room's door faced east — he went out towards the west48;
passing among the people, he attained the other world.

260Seeing this, all the people fall at [his] feet;
all the people cry out: "Glory, glory!"

261Chand Raya rose and came with [them] to his lodging,
and with joined palms bowed and fell to the ground:

262"There is no other such sinner in the three worlds:
one look at me, and all merit is used up.

263However many kinds of sin there are in the shastras —
I have committed them all, none is left.

264With such sins, how shall I, a sinner, be saved?"
Saying this over and over, he weeps, rolling at [his] feet.

265"Bearing a brahmana's body, to carry so many sins!
I fell into the intoxication of worldly things, into such delusion of maya."

266Santosha, weeping, said: "Listen, O Merciful One,
let me tell you a little about myself.

267We were born of one womb, two brothers,
and both of us sinned alike.

268There is nothing more to tell Prabhu:
our only hope is your feet.

269Make these two brahma-daityas your own;
be the lord of the life of Chand and Santosha."

270Raghavendra came and fell, rolling at [his] feet:
"With all my line I am sold [to you] — in life and in death."

271The Thakura called them, seated them beside himself
and placed his right hand on all their heads:

272"Bathe, come quickly and hear Krishna's name;
soon Gaura Bhagavan will show you mercy."

273Having bathed and put on new clothes,
they came at once before Prabhu.

274He seated all three on his left
and one by one gave the Hari-nama into their ears.

275Ramachandra Kaviraja, sitting on the left,
rolls on the ground, his whole body in ecstasy:

276"Is there anyone so merciful in the three worlds?"
Saying this, he strikes his own head with his hand.

277Seeing [this], all the Vaishnavas weep, beside themselves;
seeing it, all the people shed tears.

278The two brothers and the father prostrate themselves;
calling them, he placed his feet upon their heads.

279Such bhava at that time [no one] had seen or heard:
everywhere only the sound of weeping is heard.

280The next day, when the auspicious moment came,
at that very moment he imparted to them the mantra of Radha and Krishna.

281Another wonder also happened — hear the account:
King Yama and Chitragupta sing [his] praises.

282"I have learned that there is a purifier of the fallen in the world;
otherwise who would deliver such sinners?

283Ho, Chitragupta, see to it:
bring here the bundles of his sins."

284Chitragupta brought them and threw them into the water49:
"I know my authority is wholly gone."

285Clutching his head, the king [Yama] laments:
"Coming to earth, [he] has spread prema50.

286Everyone has gained hope of worshipping Krishna;
over whom now shall I hold authority?

287As the deliverance of the two, Jagai and Madhai, was,
[the deliverance] of these two brahmana brothers is greater still."

288When they had taken shelter at Prabhu's feet,
they brought and offered [him] many gifts:

289they gave villages, gave clothes, much gold and silver,
vessels and the like, horses, cows, [oxen]51 — by the hundred.

290From early morning there are sweets and fried dishes,
vegetable dishes, thickened milk, baras and fragrant rice.

291How great their fortune is cannot be told:
they receive the remnants of [his] plate and the water of [his] feet.

292Their fame as Vaishnavas spread through the world;
every virtue was born [in them], entering their hearts.

293Many, [coming] with them, took shelter at [his] feet;
he saved many sinners, and they found release.

294He taught them dharma according to [his] former rule;
they sit continually [at] bhajana and remembrance.

295The dharma, conduct and teaching I spoke of before [they adopted];
I shall write further of their other virtues, praising [them].

296Together with all their line they surrendered to him alone;
that they had become Vaishnavas became known everywhere.

297[Chand Raya], gathering everyone together, began to say:
"Let us go and see Gaura-raya — give your consent"52.

298Hearing this, [all] wept bitterly;
[Chand Raya's] eyes quivered and tears streamed down.

299One day, sitting [with him], the Thakura says to him:
"Listen, son Chand Raya, keep this in your heart:

300what is [rightly] yours to enjoy, enjoy;
all else — [whence come] sin and oppression — give up"53.

301Thus I have told of the deliverance of the three;
whoever hears it will attain Krishna's feet.

302Now I write the account of Chand Raya's virtues —
hearing it, people attain salvation.

303Carrying out the command, he summoned a vakil
and sent a written letter to the Nawab54.

304On receiving the letter, that hakim was afraid at heart;
all the mutsuddis began to say to him55:

305"What need is there of him?
Whoever goes to that place will lose his life."

306For fear of him, the Padshah's men did not travel that road:
they would [rather] wish for death than go there.

307One day the Thakura says in the assembly:
"It would be good for me to go home once.

308Without seeing Gaura-raya I cannot live;
I shall stay [there] some days and come back again."

309All began to consider: what is there [to say]?
What Prabhu's will is — who can say?

310They adorned ten boats with gold and jewels;
one boat was for the Thakura and his companions.

311In one boat were the two brothers, with their father among them;
in all the other boats provisions were stowed.

312They took much rice, mung and masakalai56,
and loaded many clothes and many goods.

313Many men went aboard —
all the men who take the oars.

314All the Vaishnavas who were with the Thakura
set out joyfully in the boats.

315All the household, the dwellers of the inner apartments,
all the menservants and maidservants began to weep.

316The two Raya brothers went aboard;
all together they set out by water.

317They travel by boat, talking of Krishna;
that day they halted halfway at a certain place.

318The next day, when one prahara had passed57,
they arrived and with joy at heart saw Gaura.

319Seeing him, all roll on the ground in bhava:
someone clasps [his] feet, someone is unaware of his body.

320Coming to their senses, all came and sat in their places;
the Thakura, smiling, calls [everyone] to the meal.

321Chand Raya rose and went to see the Raya58;
the Raya came out; [Chand Raya] fell at his feet.

322He, showing him honour, embraces him
and asks after everything, whether all is well.

323[Chand Raya] says: "I am a sinner, but by seeing you,
by seeing [your] feet, I have gained every blessing."

324The two came together in great love;
all together they proceeded to the Thakura.

325Having seen the arati, all, to partake of prasada,
began to sit, each in his fitting place.

326All partook of prasada in blissful rapture;
how many dishes they eat, how many [more] are served!

327The fragrance fills the nostrils, surpassing amrita;
one whispers into another's ear.

328Now and then in the midst [of the meal] they speak of Krishna:
in the middle the moon, all around the host of stars.

329Having rinsed their mouths, all sat in their places;
prasada betel was brought and given there.

330Joyfully they chewed the betel;
the devotees talk of intimate matters.

331Each performs his own sadhana in his mind.
Chand Raya says: "Fortune [is mine] — this life is praiseworthy"59.

332They brought and unloaded all the provisions from the boats
and stored them separately in the storerooms.

333At night Devidasa and his kirtaniyas60
began sankirtana before Gauranga.

334How sweet the singing, [how sweet] the sound of the mridanga!
One feels like offering up61 one's very life.

335Sri Thakura Mahashaya listens to the kirtana;
on his left is the Kaviraja, beautiful of form.

336Krishnananda Raya with all his family
relishes the song in blissful rapture.

337To his left are [Chand Raya], his father and brother;
as they listen, prema rises in their hearts.

338"Trembling and sweetness, and the artfulness of love —
seeing them, the heart breaks: I cannot forget!

339Matchless sweetness, the artfulness of love —
not for a moment can I forget [them]" (refrain)62.

340"When he, so shapely, goes off [with] the cows,
seeing and hearing [it], the soul longs to leave the body."

341Sri Thakura Mahashaya relishes [the song];
at that moment his soul weeps, and he sobs.

342His body is seen to tremble like a palm [in the wind];
now his body swells, now it shrinks.

343Tears flow from his eyes — what can I say of their measure?
Now and then he falls to the ground, lost to himself.

344Krishnananda Raya and the others roll on the ground;
how much gold, silver, clothes and shawls they gave them!

345Ramachandra Kaviraja was as if mad:
tears seemed to burst [from his eyes]63.

346The hair on his body [stood up] like the thorns of the shimul;
he lay there, [only] his heart pounding.

347Chand Raya's father and brother, hearing this,
weep for a long while, rolling on the ground:

348"O Creator, for so many days you kept [us] from this!
The soul pines — to whom shall we tell it?"

349Saying this, they weep with bitter cries:
"Only now have we come to know [this] by Prabhu's grace!"

350Trembling and trembling, they fall, not coming to themselves;
no words leave their lips, the soul is leaving [the body].

351They do not know where they are or where they go;
overwhelmed by prema, now and then they faint.

352What they say, what they do — [they only] cry, "Alas, alas!";
clutching the feet of father and brother, they roll [on the ground].

353What can I say of the measure of what they gave?
They bow to the Thakura many, many times.

354The moon of bhava rose in the palace64;
in the turmoil of bhava no one says anything to anyone.

355The kirtana ended, and all sat in their places;
the Thakura was sunk in bhava and aware of nothing.

356That night he remained in bhava, his heart overflowing;
the next day he came to himself somewhat.

357Thus for ten nights, in the rasa of talk of Krishna,
beside themselves, they knew neither day nor night.

358The next day Chand Raya took his leave
and with much humility said to the Thakura:

359"What shall I, worthless, say? What else have I?
My only hope is your two feet.

360It may seem strange, but [my] word is firm:
if I do not see Prabhu's feet, I shall give up my life"65.

361The Thakura said: "Son, [here is] the strength of my mercy:
Sri Krishna's feet are true, and all else is false."

362Saying this, he mercifully sent him off;
weeping and weeping, he goes to the Kaviraja.

363He, embracing him, says: "Blessed is this life!
You have gained all perfection — you have the shelter of [those] feet."

364[Chand Raya] gave [him] a hundred rupees and two cloths:
"Be very merciful to me, lowly one;

365[grant] the mercy that I may never forget those two feet;
regard me as your own servant."

366To all the Vaishnavas who had gone with Prabhu
he gave parting gifts, to each as was fitting.

367He went and bowed at the feet of Gauranga,
took leave of everyone and set off.

368The three boarded the boats and went to their home,
speaking of Prabhu's virtues and weeping.

369The next day they reached home in great joy;
[in] sadhana and remembrance they float ever in prema.

370Thus I have told of Prabhu's greatness;
by writing and telling, can I find its limit?

371This wondrous event is beyond people's understanding;
whoever hears of it is overwhelmed with rapture.

372Thus the two brothers live with care;
they never go against the command from Prabhu's blessed lips.

373One day, at the time of a pilgrimage to bathe in the Ganga,
Chand Raya fearlessly set out.

374Taking up to a hundred horsemen and four hundred men,
he set out with his father's consent.

375Arriving, they all bathed in the Ganga together;
there he took care to feed [everyone].

376At that time the Pathan's footmen were there66;
they went and reported everything as it was.

377Then many sepoys came and surrounded [him];
they seized Chand Raya and bound him.

378Seating him in a palanquin, they took him to the durbar;
all the way he said not another word.

379To where the Nawab sat in anger,
all the men, surrounding him, brought him.

380He went up and made his salaam; [the Nawab], seeing [him], laughed:
"What sort of hakim are you, to have plundered so much of the realm?"

381Saying this, he had him whipped67 many times;
[Chand Raya] said nothing — in his heart was joy.

382Smiling, he says: "This is a just punishment;
whatever fine68 is fitting, impose it, sir."

383He was not killed; the order was: "Keep him in the cellar"69.
On reflection, this is death while still alive.

384They took him and kept him there, [and he] fasted.
People told those at home how it had happened.

385Father, mother and kin grieved at heart:
"Find a way for him to eat."

386He writes a letter of entreaty to Prabhu;
hearing [of the trouble], the Thakura was much saddened at heart.

387The man sent [made] friends with the jamadar70;
three knew [of it], and no one else knew.

388Thus Chand Raya lives in the prison;
and here Raghavendra was utterly distraught:

389"Is there anyone who will bring me back Chand Raya?
I will give him much wealth, [even] my very life"71.

390At that time a certain man said to him:
"I will soon bring him to you," so he said.

391[Raghavendra] said: "I will give a village, a horse and a robe of honour72;
if I do not see Chand Raya, my life will leave me."

392He possessed a perfected mantra, which he knew in secret;
digging the earth and making a tunnel, he makes his way there.

393To the place where Chand Raya was kept
he made his way and came up right before him.

394Chand Raya said: "Brother, tell me,
how did you get here without coming to harm?"

395He said: "Your father told me to:
by the power of my science I will take you home."

396"How will you take me? What science do you have?"
"I will go in front, and you will go behind me.

397I have a mantra of Mother Kali;
a mantra of two and a half syllables I will speak into your ear73.

398By its power you will go — there is nothing more to fear;
come at once, do not hesitate."

399The Raya said: "Brother, how much longer shall I live?
How many offences I have committed — what is my lot!

400Thakura Mahashaya placed his foot on my head;
he is Prabhu and I am his servant, I tell you.

401In his mercy he gave the mantra of Radha and Krishna into my ears;
shall I listen to another mantra? Shame on such a life!

402Where else is there [such] a dwelling in hell?
Tell my father this request of mine:

403that Prabhu, that mantra, the hope of those feet —
by that command may I dwell wherever it may be.

404My mind is free of cares, to worship Krishna;
all the household duties — those are the heavy burden74.

405Why does my father grieve at heart?
[My] only grief is that I do not see Prabhu's feet.

406Let him not worry: my mind has become good;
the fortune is that my evil mind has not returned."

407Saying this, he chants the Hari-nama, keeping count,
and at times, sitting, sings of Krishna's virtues.

408He takes no thought for food; his thirst has left him;
at times he calls out with a bitter cry.

409As Prabhu commanded, [he practises] the sadhana of remembrance;
his mind sank into it, and there are no other thoughts.

410Whatever lila Radha and Krishna perform at whatever time,
so, in accordance with it, he contemplates in his heart.

411Now he serves, gazing on [their] faces,
now he anoints [their] bodies with kunkuma,

412now he fans [them], now he massages [their] feet —
thus his mind was absorbed in service.

413[He prays:] "Lalita, Vishakha, Chitra, Champakalatika75,
show mercy to such a one as me — [give me] more service!

414Together with your own [friends], cast a merciful glance on me,
that I may always serve and my mind remain in that.

415Rupa, Rati, Lavanga, Guna Manjari, Manjulali76,
show such mercy that I may serve together with you.

416My Prabhu Narottama — may I stay with him in that company,
and always, at [your] sign, be eager for service77.

417Wherever your dwelling is, there is my service;
keep me there always as your companion."

418Thus time passes in the sadhana of remembrance;
it turned out well — thus the net of maya fell away.

419He does not notice the days and nights pass, remaining in ecstasy.
After two or four days — what happened at last?

420One day the Nawab Sahib had [him] brought
and, filled with anger, questioned Chand Raya:

421"You, Raya, pay no money; you have plundered the whole land;
what do you have left now? Only your life.

422If you are killed, all the land's calamity will go" —
[so] resolving in his mind, he called the mahout78:

423"Bring the elephant here, maddened"79.
Many people sat down to watch the execution.

424[Chand Raya's] feet are tightly fettered; he stands.
At that moment they brought that elephant, surrounding [it].

425They brought the elephant before him — it will not stand still.
"Set the elephant on him, take his life!"

426Then [Chand Raya] remembered Prabhu Narottama:
"No more shall I see those feet that grant fearlessness!"

427They set the elephant on him; it seized him with its trunk
and at first threw him a little way off.

428When the elephant in rage seized him again,
he then grasped its trunk with both hands.

429Striking and pulling, he tore out the trunk;
with a scream the elephant crashed to the ground.

430Seeing that the elephant had died, all the people,
pressing a hand [to their mouths], began to ponder80.

431With fetters on his feet, Chand Raya stands in front;
the Nawab himself took him by the hand.

432Sitting in the durbar, he asked him:
"How much strength do you have — you killed the elephant!"

433Chand Raya said: "What strength have I?
I hold my Prabhu's command in my heart."

434"Come, tell me how it was — I wish to hear."
He told him everything from beginning to end:

435"When the Sahib had me seized and brought,
whipped and thrown into the cellar,

436then I thought of the feet of my Prabhu;
my mind decided: this is not suffering, but great happiness81.

437You yourself never inquired [about me] again;
dying of hunger, I fed on the name of Krishna.

438My father, out of love for his son, sent a man
and wrote to the mirdha to have me fed82.

439He secretly gives me a little to eat —
how much life can one keep with that?83

440For so many days I was a prisoner and did not know it as suffering:
the prison was no prison — a greater happiness than home.

441Now that I have been brought to be killed —
what strength have I? Prabhu holds the strength.

442When the elephant, not killing me, threw me aside,
at that moment I remembered Prabhu's feet.

443When the elephant came and seized me [again],
I gripped its trunk tightly with both hands.

444Knowing this, I pulled with all my might: why should I die?
Prabhu knows this — who else knows it?

445Hear one more request, sir:
if you will not take my life, if you permit [me to speak]…"

446"Speak, have no fear in your mind."
All the people say [the same] and look into his face.

447"My father sent a man to me;
by the power of perfected science he made a tunnel underneath

448and came out where I was.
Seeing him, I asked him something:

449'How did you get here, brother, without coming to harm?'
He told me he had a perfected science:

450'I have a mantra of Mother Kali; by its power I came;
by this way I will take you — such is the stratagem.

451I will give that mantra into your ear;
I will go in front, and you will go behind.'

452Hearing those words, I nearly lost my life.
Here is what I have to say:

453Prabhu gave [me] one mantra for deliverance;
giving that mantra into my ears, he bought me.

454What [else] should I hear with my ears? Shame on such a life!
After how many sins I obtained his feet!

455'Tell my father this request of mine:
I know only Prabhu's feet and nothing else.'

456This, sir, hear — it is what my heart has resolved;
at your command I have spoken it without fear."

457Softened, the Nawab embraced him;
all who were there prostrated themselves [before him].

458At once a horse was brought and a robe of honour bestowed:
"Go home right now — no one has any claim on you.

459Enjoy your own domain; I renounce everything;
I have no jurisdiction84 over it at all, I tell you."

460At once [they issued] a dastak and the Padshah's writ;
reading the paper, [Chand Raya] rejoiced at heart.

461The order was given to the munshi: "Your land,
which the Padshah had especially taken under [his] control —

462[it] was given [to you] under the panja seal together with a parwana";
all the mutsuddis came to carry it out85.

463Taking leave, the Raya sets off for home:
until he goes home, [his family's] worry will not depart.

464[But he thought:] "He at whose feet I took shelter gave me this state;
to see those feet — that is my hope."

465He sent a man, wrote a letter to his father,
and wrote to his brother to come quickly:

466"I have been released; I would have gone home,
[but first] I shall see Prabhu with joy at heart.

467You two, taking many gifts,
come at once to see Prabhu.

468We shall all meet before Prabhu;
come quickly, so that there is not a danda's delay."

469The man came, gave the letter and told the Raya [everything];
as soon as he had read the letter, he rose in haste.

470Hearing [this], Santosha Raya was overjoyed;
with many gifts and men he set out quickly.

471Meanwhile Chand Raya went to Kheturi;
leaving his horse, he then went on foot.

472The men whom [the Thakura] had earlier given him [as escort]
ran and reported to Prabhu.

473The Thakura was sitting there with the Kaviraja;
the Raya came near — [the Thakura] saw him with his own eyes.

474The Thakura, together with the Kaviraja, rejoiced:
"Such is Gauranga's play — who can understand it?"

475At that time, [while] Chand Raya [was] at the Sri Rasa-mandala86,
all the household came and told the Thakura.

476Then Chand Raya bows down;
his body thrills, tears flow from his eyes.

477He bowed many times, saying nothing;
the Thakura rose, came and embraced him.

478Seating him, he asked about everything.
"My release is only [by the mercy of] Prabhu's feet."

479He tells everything as it happened, from beginning to end;
having heard, the Thakura placed his foot on Chand's head.

480After a while people came and say:
"An army87 has come to the village," so they reported.

481[It was], as it turned out, Raghavendra Raya with his son,
who, having heard [everything], had come to see Prabhu.

482At once they went to the Thakura;
father and son bow down and offer much praise.

483The Thakura showed them mercy, placing his hand on their backs;
[there] Chand Raya saw [them] before Prabhu.

484Father and son, brother and brother greeted one another;
embracing, they wept much.

485Chand Raya said to his father's face:
"Why did you bring misfortune on yourself by this [deed]?

486Why did you send a man to take me away?" —
and he told before all how everything had happened.

487The Thakura, smiling, says, looking at Chand Raya:
"Such delightful words — for the ear [they are] life and death"88.

488Ashamed, Raghavendra bows down:
"Forgive the offence, be merciful!"

489The father is afraid of Chand Raya at heart:
"Forgive the offence, look kindly on me!"

490Father and son, speaking, took each other's hands and wept:
"We have sold ourselves to these feet — he has bought [us] with all our line."

491For five days they beheld [the Thakura], the kirtana and dancing;
the next day they made their request at Prabhu's feet,

492took leave and went to their own land, home.
[Chand Raya] rules, keeping Prabhu's command in his heart.

493After some days there came from the Nawab
an order: "Where is Chand Raya?" — so he commanded89.

494Runners went and brought Chand Raya;
with a large army he came to the meeting.

495Arriving, he met the Nawab,
who handed over to him the Ahidi pargana90.

496That day he stayed there, and in the morning [received] leave:
"In body, mind and speech no one has any claim on you."

497Having received Ahidi, the Raya goes home;
an army goes with him, music plays.

498Hear, brothers, how bhajana to Sri Krishna is done;
seeing and hearing it all, realize [it].

499Of the virtues of Sri Thakura Mahashaya [I have told] only a trifle;
I have no ability to describe them in detail.

500How he brought prema from Vrindavana,
so that all the souls on earth were flooded!

501Such bhakti of those who possess nothing as the shastras describe —
such a one who possessed nothing was Thakura Mahashaya.

502Wherever there is the business of reproach,
pride and envy are mixed into it91.

503As the guru is, so is his disciple:
by mere touch virtue is born — the essence of great jewels.

504Such is the way of sadhana, such the bhajana of the disciples;
seeing and hearing [it], the mind is amazed.

505[Through] the Acharya Thakura and Thakura Mahashaya
the prema of Chaitanya and Nitai arose.

506How many [souls] were saved through them all —
[yet] it has not touched me: grief rises in my heart.

507The Acharya Thakura showed mercy to Vira Hambira;
Thakura Mahashaya delivered Chand Raya.

508Singing [their] virtues, I bow to all
whose bhajana is the two feet of Radhika,

509on whose neck the doctrine of Sri Rupa is a necklace,
whose bhajana is the cherished desire of Gauranga's heart.

510Of all who became the Acharya Thakura's disciples
I shall describe some, the most prominent.

511The branches of Thakura Mahashaya I shall describe briefly;
little by little all the branches will become [known]92.

512One whose all is the feet of Sri Chaitanya, Nityananda and Advaita —
he obtains this wealth.

513I write this at Prabhu's command;
as Prabhu's command was, so I wrote it down in her presence.

514Whose virtues Prabhu named with her blessed lips —
those I too write down, to purify my mind.

515Sri Gopala Bhatta and Sri Lokanatha — these two;
Srinivasa and Narottama — purifiers of the fallen.

516However many their virtues — how many can be written?
I have written a little, according to my realization.

517I make my appeal to all the Vaishnava hearers:
he will find happiness whose treasure of life is Gaura.

518Let no one count what is said here as an offence of mine:
[this] was told in [my] presence by a certain Sri Guru-Vaishnava93.

519I write it at command; if anyone reviles it,
let him know: there is no offence on my part.

520Whoever accepts it incurs no offence;
but if the Gosani's command is broken, the work is in vain.

521He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the eighteenth vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.

Notes

  1. Here and below, the Prabhu at whose command the author writes is apparently Jahnava Devi, "my Thakurani" (6).
  2. That is, apparently, the author does not write of Jahnava's eternal form in the lila of Vrindavana, knowing her wish; the translation is conjectural.
  3. Ishvara Puri was Mahaprabhu's guru; Kashishvara was thus his godbrother.
  4. Pundarika Vidyanidhi was the guru of Gadadhara Pandita (cf. 16).
  5. This couplet is found only in the 1913 edition; the second line is unclear and the translation conjectural.
  6. Krishnadasa is apparently the same Krishna Pandita (26).
  7. That is, their spiritual forms in the lila (manjari names). Variant given in both editions: "Keli-kala-manjari…".
  8. Acharya Gosani is apparently Advaita Acharya. Yadunandana Acharya was the guru from whom Raghunatha Dasa received initiation.
  9. Svarupa Damodara is revered as Lalita in the lila of Radha and Krishna.
  10. The sense of the first line is unclear; apparently Raghunatha's original (siddha) nature is meant; the translation is conjectural.
  11. A yutha is a group of sakhis under one of Radha's chief friends. Variant given in both editions: "…when he met Rupa in Vrindavana".
  12. A danda is 24 minutes; a full day and night is 60 dandas.
  13. That is, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, author of the Chaitanya-charitamrita.
  14. The sense of the couplet is unclear; who the Yadunandana called "my guru" is, the text does not make clear.
  15. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 5, where Krishnadasa tells how Nityananda appeared to him in a dream and told him to go to Vrindavana.
  16. Ranga-kshetra is Srirangam on the Kaveri river, the site of the temple of Ranganatha.
  17. In other sources Gopala Bhatta's father is usually named Venkata Bhatta, and Trimalla is his brother.
  18. The chaturmasya is the four months of the rainy season, when sannyasis do not travel.
  19. Prabodhananda (Sarasvati) is here a relative of the Bhatta and Gopala's future guru (cf. 84–87).

  21. That is, the opening shlokas of the Hari-bhakti-vilasa.
  22. Apparently a reference to Sanatana's accepting Gopala Bhatta's book as his own (95): one should not judge it. The translation is conjectural.

  24. Radha-ramana is Gopala Bhatta's deity in Vrindavana.
  25. A half-shloka given in the text without a source.

  27. The sense of the second line is unclear; the translation is conjectural.
  28. What the five fruits are is not explained; possibly the four aims of life and prema.

  31. Garerhat is the region in which Kheturi lies. The second line is obscure; the translation is conjectural.
  32. That is, he held an estate yielding 84,000 [rupees] a year.

  34. The translation is conjectural ("garh-amali", "subject to the fort").

  38. A sukhpal is a kind of palanquin; the bearers are kahars.

  43. Before meeting Srinivasa, Govinda Kaviraja was a Shakta, a worshipper of the Goddess.
  44. Literally "does reviling-and-praising"; the translation is conjectural.
  45. Gaura-raya is the deity of Gauranga at Kheturi; apparently he speaks to Narottama during the night (in a dream or vision).
  46. The ululation (hulahuli, "ulu-ulu") is the auspicious cry of women in Bengal.

  48. That is, the spirit left not through the door but in the opposite direction.

  65. The translation of the first line is conjectural.

  88. The sense of the second line is unclear; the translation is conjectural.
